aiid.storage: Incident data lives in a MongoDB Atlas database (aiidprod; plus translations, history, customData). The repo is a Gatsby/Netlify site + serverless GraphQL; it does NOT ship the incident corpus.

structured_data_in_repo.what: ~306KB full taxonomy definitions (field_list, enums, descriptions) for namespaces CSETv1, CSETv1_Annotator-1/-2, GMF (Goals/Methods/Failures), MIT (Risk Domain/Subdomain incl. 2.x Privacy & Security, 4.2 Cyberattacks, Entity, Intent, Timing). Most reusable artefact for a schema/crosswalk.
Small synthetic/test seed docs (≈6 incidents) — illustrate the document schema only.
Authoritative taxonomy definitions as migration code (CSET v1, GMF, MIT AI Risk Repository mapping).
Field/value normalisation map for MIT Risk Domain/Subdomain, Entity, Intent, Timing.
1-row sample (75 columns) of MIT/severity/harm/EU-AI-Act classification import format.
Crosswalk AIID incident_id -> OECD AIM incident URL (sameAs); 2026-07-30 file has 1166 links. Useful for dedup/linking.
Documents snapshot contents: incidents.csv, reports.csv, submissions.csv, duplicates.csv, quickadd.csv, per-taxonomy classifications CSVs, plus mongodump.
Weekly AIID_Excel_Export-*.xlsx: Incidents (joined with MIT, GMF, CSETv1), Reports, Entities, Data Dictionary, Coverage Map.

aiid.security_relevance: No security-specific incident feed; security relevance comes from taxonomy classifications (MIT 2.x Privacy & Security and 4.x Malicious Actors & Misuse incl. 4.2 Cyberattacks; GMF Methods/Failures; CSET harm fields) that can filter AIID incidents to adversarial/misuse cases.

consumption.snapshot_formats: backup-YYYYMMDDHHmmss.tar.bz2 (mongodump + CSVs) and AIID_Excel_Export-<date>.xlsx, served from a public Cloudflare R2 bucket whose base URL is env GATSBY_CLOUDFLARE_R2_PUBLIC_BUCKET_URL (not hard-coded in repo); site/gatsby-site/README.md also names files aiid-backup-<timestamp>.tar.gz.
consumption.graphql_auth: Login required since 2026 (HTTP 401 API_LOGIN_REQUIRED for anonymous); use session cookie or per-account API token via "Authorization: Bearer aiid_..." (docs/API_ACCESS.md, #4070). Schema introspection remains open.
consumption.graphql_example: curl -X POST https://incidentdatabase.ai/api/graphql -H "Authorization: Bearer aiid_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"{ incidents(pagination: {limit: 3}) { incident_id title } }"}'
consumption.recommendation: For a static, offline-reproducible pipeline: download the weekly tar.bz2 snapshot (CSV incidents + classifications_MIT/GMF/CSETv1 CSVs), filter by MIT 2.x/4.x and GMF Methods for adversarial/misuse, link to OECD via oecd_relationships JSON, cite /cite/<id>. Use GraphQL (token) only for incremental updates; RSS for new-incident alerts. Vendor taxa.ts taxonomy definitions for crosswalk to ATLAS.
